newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico primary rates seen up on liquidity squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Mexico primary rates seen up on liquidity squeeze.

text.p: Traditional year-end demand for liquidity and uncertainty over trends in U.S. interest rates were seen as triggering primary hikes in Mexico, analysts and traders said on Monday.
Banco de Mexico will hold its weekly auction of government securities on Tuesday, the most sizeable portion being offered in the form of Cetes, or Treasury Certificates.
"Primary rates will have to line up with secondary levels, especially after the fallout from U.S. market volatility and the traditional year-end squeeze on liquidity," an analyst said.

Analysts forecast rises of up to 100 basis points for bellwether 28-day Cetes rates, which would place them close to 28.50 percent. Secondary rates on 28-day paper closed up 30 basis points at 28.80 percent on Monday.

"Some dealers are taking advantage of uncertainty over the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday to jack up market rates," a trader said. The FOMC will meet on Tuesday to review U.S. interest rates.

Analysts added they expected a seasonal spike in inflation during December and January to also exert upside pressure on interest rates, particularly on 91-day Cetes, which were assigned at 26.57 percent last week.
"Inflation is expected to subside in February and March, so maturities of more than 91 days will be in most demand," said another trader.
Banco de Mexico will offer 3.3 billion pesos of Cetes at 28, 91, 182 and 350 days.
